ConocoPhillips rose 1.83% today as oil prices firmed across both U.S. and global markets, with WTI crude at $82.24/barrel and Brent at $91.80/barrel. The stock has bounced back from a low of $132.19 on November 23rd, recouping losses over the past week as energy markets steadied. The timing follows geopolitical tension in the Middle East—a drone attack in Kuwait and rhetoric around Iran—which typically supports oil prices by creating supply-risk premiums.

The broader backdrop matters too: climate talks collapsed without binding restrictions on fossil fuels, which removes a near-term regulatory overhang for oil majors, while analyst coverage highlighting dividend stocks (ConocoPhillips is known for its dividend) keeps institutional interest alive in the sector.
